title: Can Modifying Data Address Graph Domain Adaptation?

problem.claim: Distribution shifts in real-world scenarios compromise GNN effectiveness and limit knowledge transfer across changing environments or domains.

gap.claim: Current UGDA efforts primarily use model-centric methods, while the potential of modifying the source graph through a data-centric approach remains underexplored.

contributions.claim: The paper revisits the theoretical generalization bound for UGDA and identifies alignment and rescaling as two data-centric principles.
The paper proposes GraphAlign, a UGDA method that generates a small transferable graph.
GraphAlign enables training a GNN on the generated graph using classic ERM for transfer to the target graph.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GraphAlign as a novel UGDA method.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that GraphAlign attains exceptional performance on the target graph when training exclusively on the generated graph.
Across various transfer scenarios, the authors report that GraphAlign outperforms the best baselines by an average of 2.16%.
The authors report that the generated graph can be as small as 0.25~1% of the original training graph.

narrative_sequence.summary: GNNs have achieved success in graph analytical tasks.
Distribution shifts limit GNN knowledge transfer, motivating UGDA from labeled source graphs to unlabeled target graphs.
Existing UGDA work emphasizes model-centric methods, but the authors identify potential in modifying the source graph.
The authors derive alignment and rescaling principles and propose GraphAlign to generate a small transferable graph.
The authors report target-graph performance gains over baselines while using a generated graph that is 0.25~1% of the original training graph.

source_observation.claim: The abstract reports that modifying the source graph according to alignment and rescaling principles supports transfer to an unlabeled target graph.

interpretation.claim: For domain adaptation, changing the data representation may address transfer limitations that are not fully resolved by changing the model.

application.claim: When facing graph distribution shifts, consider constructing a compact transferable source graph and training a standard model on it.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which transfer scenarios, graph properties, or conditions determine when this approach is effective.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact alignment and rescaling formulations.
The abstract does not identify the datasets, transfer scenarios, baselines, or statistical details behind the reported 2.16% improvement.
The abstract does not describe the generated graph construction procedure or computational costs.
